log.text: Toxic Spikes up on P1's side
Toxic Spikes ended on P1's side

decisions.rationale: Intended Mega: Blastoise. Lead Hippowdon and Blastoise to immediately override sun weather with Sand Stream and threaten fire cores with Water Spout/Earthquake. Sneasler and Choice Scarf Rotom backline clean up fast threats like Dragapult and Volcarona.
decisions.notebook: Prioritize weather control against Charizard-Y and Torkoal. Use Hippowdon's Sand Stream to neutralize sun. Keep Blastoise healthy to pressure fire types.

decisions.rationale: Charizard-Mega-Y + Torkoal lead pressures Blastoise with immediate Drought + Eruption. Toxapex walls Blastoise, Haze Calm Mind, and spreads Toxic Spikes. Dragapult outspeeds Rotom/Whimsicott, U-turn maintains momentum. Beedrill-Mega is backup late-game cleaner if Dragapult faints.
decisions.notebook: Opponent tendencies: Blastoise-Mega relies on Aura Sphere PP stall after Water Spout depletes; Whimsicott uses Encore to lock Toxapex into Haze/Recover. Strategic facts: Blastoise's Modest nature and Mega SpA investment make it difficult to tank even resisted hits; Sneasler's paralysis is irrelevant if Toxapex is the focus. Future plans: Toxapex must Haze early to prevent Blastoise from snowballing SpA boosts. Dragapult's U-turn pivots around Rotom's Trick and Whimsicott's Encore. Beedrill-Mega is reserved for late-game cleanup if Dragapult is KOed or locked out.

decisions.rationale: Hippowdon's Sand Stream already overwrote the sun, but Charizard and Torkoal are both slow sun sweepers. Blastoise mega-evolving and using Water Spout hits both foes super-effectively (2x against Charizard and Torkoal), while Hippowdon uses Rock Slide to 4x hit Charizard and 2x hit Torkoal. Protect on Blastoise is also a safe hedge if they protect or double-target it.

Maximize Sunny Day longevity. Protect scouts opponent's lead actions, avoids early Earthquake/Rock Slide OHKO on Charizard, and preserves Torkoal's Eruption for later. Mega Evolve next turn if Blastoise stays base.
decisions.notebook: Opponent's Blastoise-Mega is the primary wincon; its Water Spout under Sunny Day is still threatening but manageable if Sunny Day persists. Hippowdon's Rock Slide is a 4x OHKO on Charizard, so avoiding it early is critical. Whimsicott's Tailwind and Sneasler's FakeOut are secondary threats that can swing speed control. Toxapex must Haze Blastoise's Calm Mind boosts early to prevent snowballing. Dragapult's U-turn is a safe pivot against Rotom's Trick and Whimsicott's Encore. Beedrill-Mega remains reserved for late-game cleanup if Dragapult is locked out or KOed.

decisions.rationale: Hippowdon's Rock Slide hits both Charizard (4x) and Torkoal (2x) while Blastoise's Water Spout threatens massive spread damage on both fire-types. Since both opponents protected last turn, they cannot protect reliably again this turn.

Charizard outspeeds both foes and Air Slash Hippowdon for chip, denying it Slack Off recovery. Torkoal Eruption pressures Blastoise under Sun, forcing Protect or chip. This line pressures both foes while avoiding Rock Slide and Water Spout OHKOs. Protect scouting is less urgent after Turn 1 reveals Rock Slide.
decisions.notebook: Blastoise-Mega is the primary wincon; its Water Spout under Sun is manageable but requires chip to KO. Hippowdon's Rock Slide is a 4x OHKO on Charizard; avoid it until chip or speed control is secured. Whimsicott Tailwind and Sneasler FakeOut are secondary threats; Dragapult's U-turn is a safe pivot against Rotom Trick and Whimsicott Encore. Toxapex must Haze Blastoise's Calm Mind boosts early to prevent snowballing. Beedrill-Mega reserved for late-game cleanup if Dragapult is locked out or KOed. Prioritize Sun chip on Blastoise to enable future KOs from Charizard Solar Beam or Dragapult Draco Meteor.

decisions.rationale: Dragapult outspeeds Blastoise and threatens Draco Meteor KO after Sun chip. U-turn pivots safely if Blastoise Protects or Ice Beam threatens. Torkoal maintains Sun and pressures Blastoise.
decisions.notebook: Dragapult is the optimal pivot against Blastoise and Whimsicott Encore. Toxapex Haze is critical but can wait if Blastoise is not boosting. Prioritize Sun chip on Blastoise to enable future KOs from Dragapult or Charizard-Mega-Y. Whimsicott Tailwind is a looming threat; Dragapult's U-turn mitigates Encore risk. Hippowdon Earthquake is manageable with Torkoal's bulk under Sun.

decisions.rationale: Hippowdon uses Earthquake to KO the 12% Torkoal and heavily damage Dragapult, while Blastoise-Mega uses Ice Beam on Dragapult for a super-effective KO. Blastoise outspeeds Dragapult or trades safely, and Earthquake picks off Torkoal regardless of its action.

Sun chip on Blastoise-Mega is critical for future KOs. Draco Meteor outdamages U-turn and pressures Blastoise-Mega before it can Water Spout again. Torkoal Eruption pressures Hippowdon and Blastoise-Mega under sun, risking Torkoal but maintaining offensive momentum. Protect risks losing sun chip but is safer if Blastoise-Mega is likely to Water Spout.
decisions.notebook: Dragapult U-turn is the safest pivot against Whimsicott Encore and Sneasler FakeOut, but Draco Meteor's immediate damage on Blastoise-Mega is prioritized to enable future KOs from Dragapult or Charizard-Mega-Y. Torkoal's bulk under sun is sufficient to survive one Water Spout, but not two; sun chip is non-negotiable. Toxapex Haze is critical if Blastoise-Mega sets up, but can wait if Blastoise-Mega is not boosting. Hippowdon Earthquake is manageable with Torkoal's bulk under sun, but Rock Slide is a looming threat. Whimsicott Tailwind is a major speed control risk; Dragapult's U-turn mitigates Encore but sacrifices damage.

decisions.rationale: Toxapex avoids Blastoise-Mega Water Spout KO and Hippowdon Rock Slide chip, preserving bulk for endgame. Torkoal fainting is inevitable; Toxapex provides future utility with Haze, Toxic Spikes, and Recover.
decisions.notebook: Toxapex is the only remaining Pokémon capable of absorbing Toxic Spikes and threatening Blastoise-Mega with Scald burn. Its bulk and Regenerator make it the optimal endgame pivot against Clefable and Rotom. Prioritize Haze if Blastoise-Mega sets up Calm Mind, and use Toxic Spikes to pressure passive Pokémon like Hippowdon and Clefable. Whimsicott Tailwind remains a critical speed control risk; Toxapex's bulk under sun chip mitigates this. Avoid overcommitting to Recover unless Blastoise-Mega is sufficiently weakened.

decisions.rationale: Toxapex is alone against Hippowdon and Blastoise-Mega under Sandstorm. Hippowdon's Earthquake hits Toxapex super-effectively while Blastoise uses Aura Sphere or Protect to stay safe or deal chip damage.

Blastoise is fainted in slot b, so we must switch in Sneasler or Rotom. Bringing in Sneasler preserves offensive pressure against Toxapex with unburden/close combat options while Hippowdon earthquakes.

Toxic Spikes pressures Hippowdon and Clefable, limiting their passive recovery and forcing chip. This aligns with the endgame plan to weaken opponents for Toxapex's bulk to shine. Recover is less urgent with full HP and sun chip mitigated by Leftovers.
decisions.notebook: Toxic Spikes remains a priority to pressure passive Pokémon like Hippowdon and Clefable, especially with Blastoise-Mega weakened. Toxapex's bulk and Regenerator make it the optimal pivot for endgame, so preserving its HP is critical. Haze is reserved for Calm Mind setups, which are not yet confirmed. Whimsicott Tailwind is a persistent speed control risk, but Toxapex's bulk under sun chip and Leftovers mitigates this. Avoid overcommitting to Recover unless Blastoise-Mega is sufficiently weakened or setup is detected.

decisions.rationale: Toxapex is at 42% HP against our healthy Sneasler and chipped Hippowdon. Earthquake hits Toxapex super effectively while Sneasler can use Dire Claw to threaten poison or deal solid damage.
decisions.notebook: Toxapex is the last active foe. Ground and Poison coverage handles remaining threats.

decisions.rationale: Toxic Spikes pressures passive threats (Hippowdon, Clefable) and disrupts endgame. Hippowdon is at 39% and cannot OHKO Toxapex with Earthquake, so Toxapex survives to set hazards. Recover is unnecessary with 43% HP and Leftovers + Regenerator support.
decisions.notebook: Toxic Spikes remains a priority to cripple passive Pokémon like Hippowdon and Clefable, especially with Blastoise-Mega fainted. Toxapex's bulk and Regenerator make it the optimal endgame pivot, so preserving its HP is critical. Avoid overcommitting to Recover unless setup (e.g., Clefable Calm Mind) is confirmed or Hippowdon is weakened further. Whimsicott Tailwind is a persistent speed control risk, but Toxapex's bulk under sun chip and Leftovers mitigates this. Haze is reserved for confirmed setup, not proactive use.

reflections.summary: Blastoise-Mega's spread damage and Hippowdon's weather/ground pressure systematically dismantled the opponent's sun core and cleaned up the rest.
reflections.adjustment: Retain the effective weather-disruption and spread-damage core, but ensure faster closing against defensive pivots like Toxapex.
reflections.notebook: Opponent relies heavily on a Charizard-Y and Torkoal sun core alongside defensive anchors like Toxapex. Ground coverage and spread water damage are effective against their setup.

reflections.summary: Team-preview misalignment: Mega Charizard Y was outclassed by the opponent's Blastoise-Mega and Hippowdon core. Blastoise's Water Spout under rain (Turn 2) OHKOed Charizard and nearly KOed Torkoal, while Hippowdon's Rock Slide and Earthquake threatened immediate flinches and super-effective damage. The sun-based offensive core lacked the defensive synergy to survive early-game pressure, leading to rapid cascading faints (Charizard, Torkoal, Dragapult) before Toxapex could stabilize.
reflections.adjustment: Replace Mega Charizard Y with Mega Venusaur in Game 3. Venusaur's bulk, Thick Fat (resisting Water), and utility (Sleep Powder, Leech Seed) better counter Hippowdon and Blastoise while preserving sun for Torkoal. Adjust lead to Torkoal + Toxapex to absorb early Earthquakes and Toxic Spikes more reliably.
reflections.notebook: Opponent tendencies: 1) Hippowdon leads with Rock Slide flinch attempts, then pivots to Earthquake spam. 2) Blastoise-Mega prioritizes Water Spout under rain for early KOs, switching out after fainting a target. 3) Sneasler is a late-game cleaner with Dire Claw and Close Combat, but frail. 4) Whimsicott Tailwind is likely to support speed control, but not lead. Strategic facts: Toxic Spikes remains effective against Hippowdon/Clefable, but sun chip and sand chip reduce Toxapex's longevity. Future plans: Mega Venusaur + Torkoal + Toxapex core to counter Hippowdon/Blastoise; Dragapult as secondary speed control if Tailwind is confirmed.
